book.title: The Telegraph All New Toughie Crossword, book 1

clue.text: Drug ban gripped university class

blocks.note: to bar something is to ban it
past tense of bite, as brakes or a screw bite when they grip
U is the usual abbreviation for university
a rate is a class or grade, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: A prohibition on drugs has taken hold of a college class.
explanation.walkthrough: The book's text runs the first two words together; read 'Drug ban'. 'Drug ban' looks like one phrase, but 'Drug' alone is the definition and 'ban' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbiturates are sedative medicines, a classic example of a controlled drug.

clue.text: 'eadwear manufacturer, one bishop promoted, produces this?

definitions.text: 'eadwear manufacturer, one bishop promoted, produces this?

indicators.note: in a down clue, promoted means moved upwards, so the letters read from the bottom up

blocks.note: a hatter with the H dropped, as the apostrophe in 'eadwear signals
the Roman numeral for one
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A Cockney hat-maker wonders whether a newly elevated bishop will need one of his products.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a promoted cleric needs the square cap a hatter makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A biretta is the stiff square cap worn by Roman Catholic clergy, so a hatter might make one for a bishop.

clue.text: Again hear clergyman welcoming French and Spanish and ...

indicators.note: a host welcoming guests takes them in, so the French word goes inside the clergyman

blocks.note: RR stands for Right Reverend, a bishop's title
et is French for and
y is Spanish for and

explanation.surface: A vicar asks to hear something again while greeting French and Spanish visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dots carry the reading on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To retry a case is to have a court hear it a second time.

clue.text: Literary text hard — between Russian and Old English

indicators.note: between places one letter in the middle of the other two parts, which simply sit either side

blocks.note: Ivan is the stereotypical Russian man's name
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
OE is the abbreviation for Old English

explanation.surface: A literary passage is tough, sitting halfway between Russian and Anglo-Saxon.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivanhoe is Walter Scott's 1819 historical novel, a classic literary work.

clue.text: Classical character hoists mythical lion

indicators.note: something mythical is made up, so these letters are made up into a new order

blocks.note: to up something is to raise it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hero of antiquity lifts a legendary lion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Classical character' suggests Hercules lifting the Nemean lion; here a character is a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Upsilon is a letter of the Greek alphabet, a character used in classical Greek.

clue.text: Motorists catch ruins of sundial somewhere in Spain

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it, so the jumbled letters go inside
ruins are broken remains, so the letters are wrecked and rebuilt

blocks.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, Britain's motoring organisation
taken as written

explanation.surface: Drivers spot a broken sundial on a trip in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Andalusia is the southern region of Spain, home to Seville and Granada.

clue.text: Electronic prompt protects diary which poet writes

definitions.note: a noun phrase: the thing which a poet writes

indicators.note: protecting something means wrapping round it, so the diary word sits inside

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail
an actor's cue prompts the next line
a log is a daily record

explanation.surface: An on-screen reminder guards the journal a poet keeps.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclogue is a short pastoral poem, as in Virgil's Eclogues.

clue.text: Soldier with army eats hot bread in Asia

indicators.note: whatever eats something takes it inside, so one piece goes into another

blocks.note: a para is a paratrooper
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A soldier and his comrades tuck into some warm flatbread while posted in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: The soldier and army sit side by side, and the army swallows the hot.
explanation.definitionFit: A paratha is an unleavened, layered flatbread eaten across India and Pakistan.

clue.text: Dramatic work possible to find amongst total fakes

indicators.note: to be found amongst a group is to be inside it, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: a play is a work for the stage
poss is a short, informal form of possible
a sum is a total

explanation.surface: A drama might be discovered among a heap of forgeries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dramatic work' looks like the definition; it is the first piece, and the answer is defined by the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: To play possum is an idiom for pretending to be dead or asleep, as the opossum does.

clue.text: Equestrian worker increasingly unhappy holding animal's tail

indicators.note: holding means keeping something inside, so one piece sits within the other
a tail is the end of something, so only the last letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: the comparative of sad
the final letter of animal

explanation.surface: A stable hand grows ever more miserable while clutching a beast's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddler makes and mends saddles and harness, a trade serving horse riders.

clue.text: Gunners eat out, ordering unhealthy stew

indicators.note: ordering means arranging, so these letters are put into a fresh sequence

blocks.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners of the British Army
taken as written
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Soldiers dining out order a stew that is bad for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordering' looks like asking for food at a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratatouille is a Provencal stew of courgettes, aubergines, peppers and tomatoes.

clue.text: Eager and excited, some crossed boundary of Texas

indicators.note: something crossed is cut through, so the other letters are set across the middle of this word
a boundary is the edge, so only the outer letters of the state's name are used

blocks.note: any and some both mean an unspecified amount
first and last letters of Texas

explanation.surface: Keen and thrilled, a few people crossed the Texas state line.
explanation.definitionFit: Antsy is informal for restless and impatient, like someone with ants in their pants.

clue.text: Dawn perhaps steps on Henry

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another comes after it

blocks.note: Hal is a pet form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal
a flight is a run of stairs

explanation.surface: Someone called Dawn treads on a man named Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: Dawn looks like a woman's name; it is the time of day, given as an example by 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusk and dawn are both times of dim, partial daylight, so dawn is one example of it.

clue.text: Glittery adornment drops off back leg when dancing

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for dropping off from right to left
a dancing word moves about, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: someone who drops off falls asleep briefly
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sparkly decoration falls off the back of a dancer's leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like part of the dancer's leg, but it turns the word for dozing round.
explanation.definitionFit: A spangle is a small shiny disc sewn onto clothing to catch the light.

clue.text: Curators help artist up in arms

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
in places the reversed letters inside the weapons word

blocks.note: aid means help
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
guns are arms, weapons

explanation.surface: Museum keepers help a painter who is up in arms over something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up in arms' reads as angry; it is three separate signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A curator is a keeper of a collection, and guardians are keepers of anything entrusted to them.

clue.text: Orderly carries very big women with ease

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it within, so these pieces go inside the other

blocks.note: neat means tidy and orderly
OS means outsize, a clothing label
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: A hospital orderly lifts heavy women without any effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orderly' looks like a hospital worker but is an adjective for tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: No sweat is an informal idiom for something done effortlessly, without trouble.

clue.text: Reject oven contains uranium (extremely toxic)

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the other letters go within the oven word
extremely points to the extremes, so only the first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: an oast is a kiln for drying hops
U is the chemical symbol for uranium
first and last letters of toxic

explanation.surface: Throw out an oven that has radioactive uranium in it, which is extremely toxic.
explanation.definitionFit: Reject as a noun is a person cast aside, which is what an outcast is.

clue.text: Temporary dwelling, also, has rug left inside

indicators.note: the also word has the others within it, the way a box has contents
inside confirms the rug and left letters sit within, not beside, the other word

blocks.note: rug is slang for a wig
L is the abbreviation for left
too means also

explanation.surface: A makeshift home also contains a carpet on the left.
explanation.walkthrough: A twigloo is the shelter of bent branches built in trees by British road protesters in the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: Protest camps built these branch huts to occupy a site for weeks, so each was a short-term home.

clue.text: Assumed name initiated by new editor

indicators.note: initiated means begun, so only the opening letter of the word is used
new means made over, so the letters of the following word are rearranged
initiated by means the other part comes first, before this letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of name

explanation.surface: A pen name is launched by an editor just appointed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assumed name' reads as a pseudonym, but 'Assumed' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To try on a manner or role is to put it on for a while, as one assumes an air or guise.

clue.text: Champion to take off gold hat

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for champion, as in dog-show titles
to take someone off is to mimic them
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A winner removes a golden hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' looks like removing the hat, but here it means imitate.
explanation.definitionFit: Chapeau is the French word for hat, used in English for one.

clue.text: Floral arrangement essential in sink? On the contrary

indicators.note: in places one word inside another; the closing phrase swaps which holds which

blocks.note: the core of something is its essential part
to sag is to sink down

explanation.surface: Flowers in a vase are a must in the kitchen sink, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the essential word would go inside the sink word; 'On the contrary' reverses that, so the sink word goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsage is a small spray of flowers pinned to a dress or worn on the wrist.

clue.text: Absorb E number 144

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for number
a gross is twelve dozen

explanation.surface: A soaking-up additive has the food code E144.
explanation.walkthrough: 'E number' looks like a food additive code; it is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To engross someone is to absorb their attention completely.

clue.text: Upset diner, in tears, Knocked over domestic appliance

indicators.note: upset means knocked about, so the letters of the eater are jumbled
something knocked over ends up the other way round, so the word is read backwards
in places the jumbled letters inside the other word

blocks.note: taken as written
tears and rips both mean pulls apart

explanation.surface: A distressed diner, crying, upsets a kitchen gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tears' reads as crying but is the verb meaning rips. The jumbled diner sits inside the reversed word, just before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin drier is a household machine that removes water from washing by spinning it.

clue.text: British returning member is on a roll

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the limb and the article are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
a leg is a limb, a member of the body
taken as written

explanation.surface: A British politician heading home is on a winning streak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests a Member of Parliament and 'on a roll' a streak of success; 'roll' alone is the bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagel is a ring-shaped bread roll, boiled before baking.

clue.text: Scrap hand tool advert's dismissed

indicators.note: dismissed means sent away, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: a bradawl is a small tool for boring holes
an ad is an advert; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Throw away a hand tool once its advertisement is dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' reads as throw away but is the noun for a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is an informal word for a fight, and a brawl is a rough, noisy one.

clue.text: Everyone's entertained by tot, confronting duck

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is taken in, so one word goes inside the other
confronting means turning to face, so the word for a tot is turned round

blocks.note: everyone is all; the 's stands for is and joins the parts
a tot is a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: The whole family is amused by a toddler squaring up to a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' suggests a small child, but it is a measure of whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: The mallard is the commonest wild duck, the ancestor of most farmyard ducks.

clue.text: Tripe abruptly served with a shellfish

indicators.note: something ended abruptly is cut short, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
tripe and baloney both mean nonsense

explanation.surface: Offal is dished up hastily alongside some seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tripe' looks like offal on a menu, but it means rubbish talk.
explanation.definitionFit: The abalone is an edible sea snail, a single-shelled mollusc prized as seafood.

clue.text: Film-maker, author, adopts native verse regularly

indicators.note: adopting a child takes it into the family, so one word is taken inside the writer's name
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the poetry word is kept

blocks.note: George Orwell, author of Animal Farm
a native of a place is called its son, as in native son
second and fourth letters of verse

explanation.surface: A director who also writes takes on a local's poetry now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Orson Welles directed and starred in Citizen Kane, among the most famous film directors.
